## Verdict

Critical-framed papers are a tiny, flat slice (33 in 2017, 39 in 2025 [c1]), and the contested share fell slightly, from 10.1% early to 8.3% late [c1]. Cautionary and problem-identifying framings grew in absolute counts, but the corpus itself roughly 2.5x'd (2,743 to 6,990 [c1]).
- Decision: Treat the literature as growing and still mostly promising-framed. Do not cite a "backlash" trend. Any claim about quality or validity needs a separate review of the papers.
- Confidence: medium - one corpus and one classifier, with orientation labelling how a paper frames its finding, not whether it is right [c1]. The window ends 2025.
- What would change it: Per-year shares of critical, cautionary and problem-identifying papers rising across 2026 data, or a manual audit showing the labels miss critique.

## What the data shows
- Window 2017-2025, 20,812 papers, six phrases expanded from "mindfulness" [c1].
- Yearly volume rose from 2,743 (2017) to 6,990 (2025) [c1].
- Critical-orientation papers: 33 (2017), peak 55 (2023), 39 (2025). Total 345, which is 1.6% of the browsed subject [c1][c2]. Late-vs-early-third ratio is 1.32, against 2.01 for promising [c1].
- Cautionary rose from 60 to 205 (late/early 2.76; CAGR 16.6%) [c1]. Problem-identifying rose from 172 to 366 (late/early 1.29) [c1]. Breakthrough rose from 53 to 230 [c1].
- Promising is the largest class, with 11,518 papers in the stance totals [c1]. The browse facet shows 23,174 (56.0%) across the wider matched set [c2].
- Contested share: 9.7% (2017), 8.3% (2023), 7.9% (2024), 8.7% (2025) [c1]. Early-vs-late is 10.1% vs 8.3%, a delta of -1.8 points; Prism reads this as "broadly unchanged" [c1].
- Positive share moves without direction: 31.0% (2017), 24.1% (2019), 34.9% (2024), 29.1% (2025) [c1].
